name: FieldAI
description: FieldAI is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, the investors and SPVs that hold its shares, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: FieldAI is a privately held robotics software company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $314 million Series A-1 round announced on August 20, 2025, valued the company at $2 billion.

Founded in 2023 and based in Irvine, California, FieldAI develops AI software intended to serve as a single control system for many kinds of robots, from four-legged machines to humanoids. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions, frequently through special purpose vehicles, and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.

table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round. FieldAI announced $405 million raised across the two rounds without disclosing the amount or valuation of each; the figures shown are as reported by Reuters and TechCrunch.
round_notes: FieldAI disclosed both rounds for the first time on August 20, 2025, when it announced that it had raised $405 million in two consecutive financings.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Bezos Expeditions, Prysm and Temasek co-led the Series A-1, with participation from Khosla Ventures, Intel Capital, Nvidia's NVentures, Canaan Partners, BHP Ventures and Emerson Collective. Earlier investors include Gates Frontier and Samsung.
spv_sentence: Since 2025, three special purpose vehicles formed to invest in FieldAI have filed with the SEC, one of them in 2026.
sources: Sources: FieldAI's announcement of its Series A and Series A-1 (August 20, 2025); reports by TechCrunch (August 2025), Reuters (August 2025), SiliconANGLE (August 2025) and Orange County Business Journal (September 2025); and SEC Form D filings.
